## 2. Theorems and derivations

**Parity theorem — there is no mean-field part.** Sources: W3 §3, BN K3c, HTML §5.2.
- Take a source born at layer b. At any later layer l, its legs are P = Wᵀ D P′ and A = P a_b.
- H, T2, T3, T4 and D3 are linear in the source's κ₃, so they are **odd** in W^(l).
- C, the leg Grams and the per-neuron variances are **even** in W^(l).
- The weight ensemble is sign-symmetric, so E[H_s | C, Grams, history] = 0 exactly.
- Consequences:
  - Closures built only from even statistics drop the whole contribution. The measured failures of such closures are 9.1e-7 and 2.3e-6.
  - Replacing a source by its expectation has an error floor of √(6/(r+8)): 12% at r = 384 and 16% at r = 224.
  - κ₄ terms built from two κ₃ factors are even, and C⊗C is the only even invariant available. This explains the empirical law G_off = λ_l C_off.
- Status:
  - The argument came from a Fable 5 consultation and was checked by us.
  - The floor was derived independently by two other models (W3 §3).
  - HTML still marks the derivations "hand-check" (not yet verified by hand).

**Algebraic floor** (BN K3c, Fable). Exactly evaluating one old source's D21 costs at least min(2n²r, 4nr³) per source-layer.

**Spherical identity (V31).** Sources: W3 §9, BN K3n, HTML §2.
- Write X = (R/√n)Y, with Y uniform on the sphere and R ~ χ_n independent of Y.
- The bias-free ReLU net is degree-1 homogeneous, so E[h(X)] = a₁E[h(Y)].
- a₁ = √(2/n)Γ((n+1)/2)/Γ(n/2) = **0.99975589**.
- Y has C = I, κ₃ = 0 and κ₄ = c·Sym₃(I⊗I) with c = −2/(n+2). In the chain's core representation this is g_prev = −6/(n+2).
- Checks:
  - The injection's scale shift is +2.450e-4, against +2.442e-4 predicted by the identity (0.3% agreement).
  - The control without a₁ (ang_noa1) gives 8.02e-8.
  - Kaggle, 10 MLPs: −0.5%. Grader: −1.1% raw.

**No compressed linear state is closed under transport** (BN K3aj; W3 §11.10).
- Sym³ is an irreducible GL(n) representation. A linear state closed under every dense M^(⊗3) therefore needs C(n+2,3) ≈ 1.8e8 numbers.
- Our caveat: with fixed, known M, the relevant bound is what future readouts can observe, at most n² per remaining layer.
- Wording correction (BN K3al): this is a count of the known contraction orders, not a lower bound on arithmetic cost.

**Dual contraction orders** (BN K3aj).
- The "lazy cubic circuit" in reverse mode costs about 4l products at depth l, about 245 u in total. The source chain costs 249 u. These are dual orders of one tensor network.

**Exact structure of the births** (BN K3l, K3j, K3al Round 10).
- A_s = P_s·diag(w1_b)·C_off^(b), exactly, at 1e-5 at every slot and layer. Its diagonal is zero and its spectrum is flat (r99 = 310–809).
- Correction: A = P R_b with a fixed full n×n birth matrix R_b, fitted to 1e-14.
- Both P legs of a source are the propagator T_b.
- The born tensor has two families (BN K3q):
  - AAP: |AAP|/|total| = 0.36–0.37.
  - MPP: |MPP|/|total| = 0.74–0.75.
  - cos(AAP, MPP) = +0.56–0.57, and MPP carries 2.6–2.7× the D3 diagonal.

**Edgeworth port deficit** (BN K3ae; W3 §11.4).
- The newborn Sym(X1⊗I⊗Y1) carries exactly half of both K×C all-distinct families.
- Regression coefficients: −0.55 to −0.69 and −0.6 to −0.9, against −1/2 predicted.
- The full fix S = 2 gives +3.4% / +3.1%. S = 1.25 gives −0.8% / −0.35%.
- The fitted curve E(t) = 1 − 0.034t + 0.068t² has its optimum at t = 0.25, worth −0.43% (Astra, BN K3ah).

**Meaning of λ** (BN K3x, K3y, K3ab).
- λ_l equals the mean of b_l·κ₄(i)/var(i) to within 2% (6.8e-3 vs 6.9e-3 at L15).
- But λ fits the r = 1 harmonic core (pre-activation R² ≥ 0.95 from layer 3), not the raw slice (F105).
- The true slope of K31 on C_off is 1.3–1.55e-2. The chain uses 0.69–1.0e-2.

**Mean-error gain per layer** (BN K3ab). The inherited mean error passes with gain |W row|²E[Φ²] = 0.65 at layer 2, rising to 0.8–0.96 at depth.

**Tolerance law** (BN G3.1, K3h). Extra final MSE ≈ 4.2e-6·ε², where ε is the relative RMS error of D21. So D21 must be right to about 2%.

## 3. Error map: which channels carry the error

**The closures are exact given true inputs.**
- Edgeworth mean closure on the teacher's true marginals: 9.3e-11 at L16, and 5e-11 to 1.5e-10 at every layer (BN K3ab; W3 §11.1).
- The per-layer chain MSE accumulates from 0.7e-9 at L1 to 2.29e-8, adding about 1–2.5e-9 per layer (BN K3ab).

**Channel oracles: true value injected into the mean closure at every layer** (MLP #0, plain chain 2.290e-8; BN K3ad, W3 §11.2).

| exact input | final MSE | ratio |
|---|---|---|
| variance | 1.220e-8 | 0.533 |
| κ₄ diagonal | 1.600e-8 (1.609e-8 in K3ac) | 0.699 / 0.702 |
| κ₃ diagonal | 1.965e-8 | 0.858 |
| variance + κ₃ | 0.817e-8 | 0.357 |
| variance + κ₃ + κ₄ | 0.130e-8 | 0.057, which is the truth's noise floor |
| true κ₄ everywhere *except* the mean closure | 2.311e-8 | ≈1, i.e. no gain |
| κ₄ diagonal + (2,2) + (3,1) slices | 1.738e-8 | 0.759 |
| (3,1) slice only / (2,2) only / both | 2.353 / 2.796 / 2.680e-8 | 1.027 / 1.221 / 1.170 |

- Opus 12 replication (BN K3am): ratios 0.532 / 0.865 / 0.702 / 0.057.
- Opus also notes that single-channel ratios are **upper bounds**, because they include inherited error.

- Pre-activation mean 1.84e-8 (80%), variance 2.0e-9, κ₃ᵢᵢᵢ 1.0e-9, κ₄ᵢᵢᵢᵢ 1.0e-9.
- The fresh error per layer goes from 0.3e-9 at L2 to 4.4e-9 at L16.
- At depth the fresh error splits about 50% variance, 25% κ₃, 25% κ₄. Fit coefficients are −0.99, −0.98, −1.04 against a theoretical −1, with R² 0.93–0.97 from L9 on.

- 2.24e-8 → 4.2e-9. About 80% of the final error is inherited mean error.

**κ₃ slice error** (BN K3ad, K3ae).
- Slope 1.00, R² 0.996–0.998, random error 4.1% at L3 rising to 6.7% at L15.
- 91–96% of it is in the **all-distinct** post-ReLU κ₃ entries. Relative to themselves those entries are 9–16% wrong.
- It is **not truncation**: running with no confinement leaves the slice error at 6.6% and lowers the final MSE only −3.9%, for +19% cost (util 0.248 → 0.294).
- About 55% of it is unexplained even at second order in K. The 12 K×K terms have rms 3e-6 to 2e-5, against an error of 2.2e-4 (BN K3ag).

**κ₄ diagonal** (BN K3ac, K3ad, K3al).
- Pairwise transport of the true post-ReLU slices gets the level right (slope 1.00) but not the pattern (corr 0.24–0.59).
- The next layer's κ₄ diagonal is about 90% the (2,2) pair term.
- Even with exact (4), (3,1) and (2,2) slices, the next diagonal is 14 / 22 / 33 / 43 / 46% wrong at L4 / L8 / L12 / L15 / L16.
- The next d3 comes 90–99% from off-diagonal κ₃. The diagonal-to-diagonal channel is only 18 / 6 / 3 / 1.8 / 1.7% in norm.

**κ₄-gap oracle** (BN K3as, K3at; W3 §11.11).
- The full chain with the true κ₄ diagonal goes 2.29e-8 → **1.61e-8**, the leaders' raw range.
- The teacher *pattern* rescaled to the chain's level gives 1.551e-8, which is 108% of the gain. A 50% blend gives 74%, and layers ≥ 8 only give 86%.
- The same oracle on cheaper κ₃ chains:
  - AGE_OLD 2: ×0.88.
  - + R_OLD 256/128: ×0.97.
  - AGE_OLD 1 + 192/96: ×1.02.
  - So "cut κ₃, recover with κ₄" is closed.

**One-step closure floors** (BN K3t; 2e8 samples per layer). RMS error of the next-layer mean:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Gaussian h | 5.2e-4 | 5.1e-4 | 4.6e-4 | 4.5e-4 |
| B: copula with exact marginals | 1.14e-3 | 9.2e-4 | 8.1e-4 | 7.5e-4 |

The Gaussian one-step closure errs at about 3× V29's final error (1.5e-4 rms). The copula with exact marginals is worse than the plain Gaussian closure at every layer, so the copula family is dead.

**Learned residual, V33** (BN K3v; 100 MLPs, 102,400 neurons). Baseline residual MSE 2.2049e-8.

- A per-MLP offset explains 0.44% of the residual variance.
- Every single feature has correlation ≤ 0.04 with the residual.
- Q19 online mean correction refit: in-sample R² 0.15 at L3 and 0.02 at L8/12/15, against a chance level of about 0.013 (BN K3am).

## 0. Ground truth any architecture must respect

- **Channel oracles** (true values fed into the mean closure): variance −47%, κ4 diagonal −30%, κ3 diagonal −14%, all three −94% (UI R26; Q headroom). Forcing the true mean: −81% (PL).
- **Closure exactness:** the closures are exact given true inputs (UI R22: 9e-11; Q5). The error is in the input channels, accumulated over depth.
- **κ3 memory:** carried over at least 10 ages. Keeping h ages gives L15 error h2 84%, h4 65%, h6 46%, h8 31%, h10 16% (KA A17). It is not low-rank, and linear compressions closed under transport are dead (KA A01–A09, A17).
- **κ4 oracle:**
  - Full chain with the true κ4 diagonal: 2.290e-8 → **1.609e-8 (×0.702)**, which is the leaders' raw MSE.
  - With cheaper κ3 chains the oracle helps less: ×0.876 (AGE_OLD 2), ×0.966, ×1.024 (R14 §3).
  - So "cut κ3, recover with κ4" is CLOSED.
- **κ4 pattern facts:**
  - Exact linear carry of the true κ4 tensor gives corr 0.77–0.80 (PA §1; R16).
  - One step from the true (4) + (3,1) + (2,2) slices gives only 0.30–0.45 (R16).
  - Chain baseline corr 0.26–0.34 at L12–16.
- **Cost floor:** the young tier needs 193 square products (98.4 u) in every contraction order (KA A15). The "Sym³ / Khatri-Rao wall" closes linear κ3 compression (PA §4; MA C2).

- **What the unfair kills had in common.** All 8 REVIVED kills were cost or knob levers, never architectures (KA §2). They came from five mechanisms:

candidates.name: 3. Lagged-vertex D21 hub: exact kappa3->kappa4 conversion births (Q1 C.T) from the chain's own kappa3 sources
candidates.mechanism: New birth channel. At a ReLU vertex m, the He2 piece of the response converts INCOMING kappa3 into kappa4: kappa(z_a^2, z_b, z_c, z_d) = 2(C_ab T_acd + C_ac T_abd + C_ad T_abc). Its diagonal readout at target t is q_j(i) = 24 sum_a g_a P_ai X_ai S~_j(i,a), with m = t-j, g = phi/(2 sigma) at m, and P, X = the young legs of the slot born at m (already used by the V56 star). The new state is S~_j(i,a) = kappa3(z_i^t, z_i^t, z_a^m), a cross-layer kappa3 slice. Cheap construction, a re-association of the existing hub: D21 = sum_k LA_k A_k^T + LP_k P_k^T. The exact birth law A_k = P_k R_k (BN K3al) and the linear transport P_k(t) = M^T P_k(t-1), M = diag(Phi)W, give D21 = S_1 M with S_1 = [hub with right factors at t-1] + LA_new A_birth^T + LP_new (the newborn slot needs ONE product instead of two). So S~_1 comes out as an intermediate, and the extra telescoping product S_1 M is paid for by the newborn's saved product. Old-tier sources join S_1 by lifting their 'inner' with the t-1 basis Qc_{t-1} (direct lift at join layers). Stage 2 extends to lags 2-3 the same way (store legs/bases h layers back; one telescoping product per lag, offset by newborn savings).
candidates.why_promising: Today's analysis of the stored set-C arrays shows that the deep kappa4 pattern is NOT additive over birth ages. The cross-age interaction of nonlinear vertices with older non-Gaussian history is worth ~0.1 corr, and Q1 conversion is the one such interaction whose readout is FLOP-neutral to compute exactly. It also runs on the chain's kappa3, which already carries the cubic e-term dressing that the K=2 Monte Carlo lacked.
candidates.evidence_for: Measured today (scratchpad/arch_tests/claude_superpos2.py on data/kaggle_out/r17_ceiling_c/r17_hermite_family_ceiling_C.npz, teacher kaggle/r17/data/r17_data.npz). candidates.name: 4. Cubic-vertex TT births: the kappa3 x kappa3 term of the He3 response, read through lagged cross slices
candidates.mechanism: From the verified identity kappa(u_a^3, u_b, u_c, u_d) = ... + 3(T_abc T_aad + T_abd T_aac + T_acd T_aab) + ... (r17_curvature_identities.json, 8.1e-16). At vertex m = t-j, with c3 = -alpha phi/(6 sigma^2): tt_j(i) = 3*4 sum_a c3_a P_ai S~_j(i,a) Y_j(a,i). Here S~_j is the lagged cross slice from candidate 3 and Y_j(a,i) = kappa3(z_a^m, z_a^m, z_i^t) is the vertex layer's (2,1) slice carried forward. Y_j = D21_m (Phi P^{(j)}) is formed once at the vertex layer and telescoped Y_j(t+1) = Y_j(t) M_t, one product per lag per layer. It enters as one more V56 map feature (fed to the mean closure only).
candidates.why_promising: In the Hermite Monte Carlo, the joint quadratic+cubic family far exceeds either alone: K=3 0.848/0.799/0.817, K=2 0.548/0.449/0.530, orders 0,1,3 0.511/0.498/0.469. So mixed c2-c3 diagrams carry much of the pattern, and TT (two c2-born kappa3 meeting a c3 vertex) is the lowest-order such kappa4 birth. It reuses candidate 3's S infrastructure, so once that exists the marginal engineering is small.

The cubic star by itself (HTQB star_h6 0.521/0.489/0.471, round18_htqb.json) roughly equals the cubic-only Monte Carlo (orders 0,1,3: 0.511/0.498/0.469). Cubic-only adds nothing beyond the star, so the cubic surplus in K=3 must come from c3 vertices acting on c2-born non-Gaussianity (TT and C.K dressing). Today's set-C additivity gap (+0.11-0.14 joint vs additive windows) is the envelope this term competes for. Free star-leg contractions are dead (measured today, claude_perage.py): per-age star groups 0.693, star (2,2)-row-sum proxy 0.692, linear star 0.693, vs 0.694 base. So the cubic-vertex gain has to come from genuinely new kappa3-dependent contractions like TT.
candidates.closest_dead_idea_and_why_different: Dead: R15 source-resolved skew energy E_i = sum_b B_bi^2/v^3 (adds <= 0.004 corr) and the D2 kappa3 x kappa3 covariance patches (rms 2-3e-6 vs error 6.5-9e-5). Also the memoryless 'two kappa3 factors are even -> lambda C_off' law. Difference: E_i was a diagonal per-source energy, and the patches targeted the covariance channel. TT is the exact cubic-vertex kappa4 birth, contracted over all vertex neurons with cross-layer slices, and aimed only at the kappa4-diagonal pattern in the mean closure, which is the channel with the 1.61e-8 oracle.
candidates.expected_gain: Untested. Estimate in-map rho +0.01 to +0.05 on top of candidate 3, i.e. raw -0.5% to -2.8%. Net score roughly 0% to -2% after its product cost (estimate). Run it only if set-D attribution (candidate 3, test b) shows a cubic-vertex interaction share >= 0.03.
candidates.cost_estimate: +1 n^3 product per lag per layer for the Y telescope (about 0.6 u Strassen or 1.0 u plain): lag 1 over L6-15 is ~6-10 u (+3-5% util); ops +1.1-2.4k (Strassen) or ~+10 (plain). This cost is why it needs >= +0.05 rho to pay.
candidates.ceiling_test: Same Kaggle GPU Monte Carlo as candidate 3(a), also accumulating Y_j(a,i) = E[(z_a^m-mu_a)^2 (z_i^t-mu_i)] (an n^2 accumulator per (t,j)). Build tt_j with teacher c3 and P. reviews.overlaps_dead_idea: Partly. reviews.numeric_errors: All the corr numbers are verified. Per-layer corr ignores contrast after the rescale to layer-mean level: the V55 s3sq x0.8 sweep cost +1.24%, so an intercept that varies with depth could shift contrast in an untested direction. If the deployed LMIN is below 6, the l/16 term extrapolates below the fitted range.
